text:
claire: Not sure if anyone else has seen this — swift-ios sample (sdk-swift 0.3.0) is printing raw emails and API tokens to the Xcode device log during the background token refresh flow. The odd bit: the retry generates a new trace id so the initial unredacted line doesn't correlate with the later redacted retry log.

claire: repro (simulator):
```
cd examples/ios && swift run ExampleApp
# tap 'Call (expire token)'
# watch device logs in Xcode
```

claire: snippet from device log:
```
2026-06-02 12:04:01.220 ExampleApp[12345:678901] ERROR network: request failed user=kelly@startup.io x-rw-session=sess-77A
2026-06-02 12:04:01.421 ExampleApp[12345:678901] INFO retry attempt=2 trace=00-abc-123-01 x-rw-session=sess-77A
2026-06-02 12:04:01.501 ExampleApp[12345:678901] ERROR network: request failed user=[REDACTED] trace=00-def-456-01 x-rw-session=sess-77A
```

ben: interesting that x-rw-session stays stable here, but trace changes. looks like the retry path spins up a fresh span which is why our otel context-based redaction doesn't catch the first line.

opes: two things to tackle: (A) redactHook init race — on iOS we fetch remote redact rules async to keep binary small; that leaves a startup window where os_log prints raw PII, (B) our logger shim only patches os_log at error/warn; the auth flow uses os_log(.debug) and os_trace which are unpatched.

opes: immediate mitigation ideas: ship a tiny baked-in rule set for common PII patterns (emails, sk-*, jwt fragments) that is applied synchronously during SDK init; also expand the logger shim to cover debug/trace in sampleapps.

sam: for correlation, ensure the request-level attempt id is created once at attempt start and stamped into both `x-rw-session` and `x-request-id` headers, and then reused for retries. The SDK's retry layer currently calls `generateTrace()` per attempt which explains the trace flip.

ivy: additional nuance: on iOS the system logging (os_log) and stderr can be reordered because background threads log to unified logging; that makes it look like the redacted line happened before the unredacted one in some captures. We should capture logs with a deterministic wrapper during tests (intercept OSLog via a local logging adapter) to avoid ordering flakiness.

claire: plan I'm going to PR in examples/ios: 1) preload a small built-in redactRules.json and apply it synchronously; 2) extend the logger shim to patch os_log for debug/trace in debug builds; 3) add XCTest that runs expired-token path, captures logs (via adapter), and asserts no email-like or sk- token regex in captured output.

ben: for sdk-swift change: 1) retry middleware should compute `attemptId = headers["x-rw-attempt"] ?? UUID()` once and attach it to every attempt; 2) avoid spawning a new span on retry unless user asks for a fresh span — keep parent span bound. Add unit tests for both behaviors.

opes: note about performance: if we patch debug/trace in production it can be expensive; make it opt-in via `TelemetryOptions(redactOnAllLevels: Bool)` defaulting to false for release builds. Examples/dev should enable it.

log-bot: Please open GH issue with labels: `devex, telemetry, security` and attach the captured device logs. Recommend severity: high for sampleapps due to PII exposure.

ivy: tests: XCTest should not just grep for emails; use `NSRegularExpression` to look for both email patterns and `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{8,}` tokens, fail early if found. Also add a small CI job that runs the iOS example in simulator and fails the build when the regex matches.

claire: I'll implement the example PR and a companion sdk-swift PR. Repro env: Xcode 15.4, swift 5.9, sdk-swift 0.3.0, otel-swift 1.5.0. I'll ping when PRs are up. :thumbsup:

ben: small follow-up: document interactions with Sentry/sampling integrations — some customers use Sentry and we need to ensure our redaction happens before any downstream error exporters snapshot log context. Add a note in telemetry README.

opes: thanks everyone. I'll add the `attemptId` invariant to the SDK retry spec and flag an internal RFC so other language SDKs follow the same header naming.

claire: filing issues and PRs now. tagging @security for visibility.
